previous_disclosures.summary: On August 17, 2024, AMD agreed to acquire ZT Systems for approximately $3.4 billion in cash and stock, with potential additional payments of $300 million and up to 740,964 shares, expected to close in the first half of fiscal year 2025 subject to regulatory approvals.

current_disclosures.summary: AMD completed the $3.2 billion acquisition of ZT Systems in March 2025, then sold the ZT Manufacturing Business to Sanmina for $2.4 billion plus stock in October 2025, retaining the ZT Design Business; AMD is eligible for up to $450 million in contingent consideration and Sanmina is the preferred manufacturing partner for complex AI solutions.

comparisons.peer_topic: Strategic Focus on Leadership and Acquisitions
comparisons.peer_summary: The company's strategy focuses on technology leadership and category-leading solutions, achieved through strategic acquisitions and extensive internal research and development to drive diversified and sustainable results.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Avago explicitly identify strategic acquisitions as a core component of their strategy to maintain technology leadership and expand infrastructure capabilities. AMD describes acquiring ZT Systems to extend data center infrastructure capabilities and accelerate AI solutions, while Avago states it seeks to achieve technology leadership through strategic acquisitions of businesses and technologies alongside internal R&D.

sentences.text: We also focused on extending our data center infrastructure capabilities by entering into an agreement in August 2024 to acquire ZT Group Int'l, Inc. (ZT Systems), a provider of AI and general purpose compute infrastructure for hyperscale computing companies.
We believe that with the acquisition of ZT Systems, we can accelerate time to market for our leadership AI training and inferencing solutions.

Our strategy is focused on technology leadership and category-leading semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions delivering a comprehensive suite of innovative infrastructure technology products to the world's leading business and government customers.

We seek to achieve this through strategic acquisitions of businesses and technologies, as well as extensive internal research and development, to ensure our products retain their technology market leadership.

comparisons.peer_topic: Network and Edge (NEX) Strategic Transformation and Market Growth
comparisons.peer_summary: NEX aims to transform networks and edge compute systems into general-purpose platforms running cloud-native software on programmable hardware, leveraging core strengths in compute, connectivity, software, and manufacturing to grow traditional markets and accelerate entry into emerging ones.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Intel describe strategic initiatives to transform data center and edge infrastructure for the AI era. AMD pursues this through the acquisition of ZT Systems to extend hardware infrastructure capabilities for hyperscale computing. Intel describes a strategic transformation within its Network and Edge (NEX) segment to turn networks and edge compute into general-purpose platforms running cloud-native software on programmable hardware, leveraging its manufacturing and design strengths.

sentences.text: We also focused on extending our data center infrastructure capabilities by entering into an agreement in August 2024 to acquire ZT Group Int'l, Inc. (ZT Systems), a provider of AI and general purpose compute infrastructure for hyperscale computing companies.
We believe that with the acquisition of ZT Systems, we can accelerate time to market for our leadership AI training and inferencing solutions.

NEX aims to transform the world's networks and edge compute systems from fixed-function hardware to general-purpose compute, acceleration, and networking devices running cloud native software on programmable hardware.
We are leveraging our core strengths in compute, connectivity, software, and manufacturing at scale to grow traditional markets and to accelerate entry into emerging ones.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company experienced substantial improvements in pricing and margins in 2024, driven by increased demand growth partly from AI deployment, normal customer inventories, and industry supply discipline.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address the impact of AI deployment on the semiconductor market dynamics, though from different perspectives. AMD focuses on its strategic move to acquire infrastructure capabilities (ZT Systems) to better serve the AI market and accelerate time-to-market. Micron focuses on the resulting market conditions in 2024, noting that increasing demand growth driven in part by AI deployment contributed to substantial improvements in pricing and margins for memory and storage products.

sentences.text: We believe that with the acquisition of ZT Systems, we can accelerate time to market for our leadership AI training and inferencing solutions.

Increasing demand growth, driven in part by deployment of AI and mostly normal customer inventories, combined with industry-wide supply discipline, resulted in an industry supply and demand balance that substantially improved from 2023 conditions.

comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center Revenue and AI Inference
comparisons.peer_summary: Data Center revenue for fiscal year 2024 was $47.5 billion, up 217% from fiscal year 2023, with approximately 40% estimated to be for AI inference. In the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2024, large cloud providers represented more than half of this revenue.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures discuss the strategic importance of data center infrastructure in the context of AI, but focus on different aspects of the value chain. AMD highlights a vertical integration strategy by acquiring ZT Systems to provide compute infrastructure for hyperscale companies and accelerate its AI training and inferencing solutions. In contrast, Nvidia discloses financial performance metrics for its Data Center segment, noting that AI inference accounted for approximately 40% of revenue, highlighting the market demand for the very AI solutions AMD aims to accelerate through acquisition.

comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm believes that 5G, combined with high-performance computing and on-device AI, will drive adoption in automotive and IoT sectors, and that maintaining leadership in 5G technology development, standardization, and IP licensing is critical for long-term business sustainability.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies discuss the role of AI in driving future technology adoption, but apply it to different end markets. AMD focuses on AI training and inferencing solutions for data centers and hyperscale computing via its acquisition of ZT Systems. Qualcomm focuses on the convergence of 5G, high-performance computing, and on-device AI to drive adoption in sectors like automotive and IoT, emphasizing its leadership in standardization and licensing.
